study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Ma et al., Journal of Behavioral Addictions, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Comparative analysis of cortical anatomy in male participants with internet gaming disorder or tobacco use disorder: Insights from normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: 665 healthy control (HC) participants were obtained from the Brain Genomics Superstruct Project (GSP), a large-scale, multi-site brain imaging study. 78 male IGD and 80 male TUD participants were enrolled locally from the Center for Cognition and Brain Disorders at Hangzhou Normal University (single-site recruitment). After quality control and matching, the final sample was 665 HC, 68 IGD, and 71 TUD.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "data of 665 male participants were downloaded from the Brain Genomics Superstruct Project (GSP), a large-scale, multi-site brain imaging study (Holmes et al., 2015)" ... "78 male individuals with IGD and 80 male individuals with TUD were enrolled in this study"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Ma2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Participants, L71

answer.GSP: healthy control reference cohort for normative model construction (10-fold cross-validation training/testing)

answer.SINGLE-SITE: clinical transfer data (IGD and TUD patient groups for deviation analysis from the normative model)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The GSP dataset provided 665 HC participants used to estimate the normative model of cortical thickness via 10-fold cross-validation using Gaussian process regression. The locally recruited IGD (n=68) and TUD (n=71) participants were then evaluated against this normative model to quantify individual deviations (Z-scores).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The normative range of the model in the HC group was estimated through 10-fold cross-validation and then applied to patients"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Ma2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative modeling, L107

model-1.model-name: Gaussian process regression normative model for cortical thickness

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was constructed using GPR with 10-fold cross-validation on 665 HC participants from the GSP dataset. In each fold, approximately 598-599 participants (9/10) would be used for training and 66-67 for testing, but the exact per-fold numbers are not explicitly reported.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The quality control process conducted based on weighted average image quality rating (IQR) and Euler index yielded a final sample of 68 participants in the IGD group, 71 participants in the TUD group, and 665 participants in the HC group" ... "The normative range of the model in the HC group was estimated through 10-fold cross-validation"

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are reported for the overall HC group (n=665) in Table 1. The study used 10-fold cross-validation, so the training phase in each fold would use approximately 9/10 of the HC data, but per-fold age statistics are not reported separately.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The study exclusively included male participants. The title states 'male participants' and the Methods section specifies '804 male participants (665 healthy individuals, 68 IGD and 71 TUD)'. Therefore all 665 HC used in the normative model are male. Per-fold train-phase sex breakdown is not separately reported but would be 100% male as well.
